A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DiOpt and the same underlying research despite the changed title. All 31 pages of each version, including equations, tables, figures and appendices, support comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original benchmark results, training dynamics and sensitivity experiments in Section 6 and Appendices D–F.

after.justification: v4 reports original benchmark results, component ablations, training-time measurements and sensitivity experiments in Section 6 and the appendices.

M1.justification: The supervised warm start, weighted bootstrapping, alternating reset, lookup table, equality completion and inference selection are retained. Expanded Newton-completion explanations and revised notation document the existing procedure; the penalty-weighting variant is an experimental comparator.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the two-dimensional toy problem, QP, QPSR, CQP, ACOPF57, ACOPF118 and SMPL-to-H1 motion retargeting. QP moves into v4 Appendix E; it is not removed from evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v4 adds explicit IPOPT reference rows and includes supervised diffusion alongside DC3 and MBD in the main comparison. Its RectFlow rows represent the retained diffusion baseline used as a proxy, not a newly implemented RectFlow model. MLP results and MBD-without-completion comparisons disappear, while a penalty-weighting comparator is added.

E3.justification: v4 Table 6 specifies 100 diffusion steps and 10,000 epochs for main experiments, replacing v2's five-step exceptions for Retargeting/ACOPF118 and 5,000-epoch exception for ACOPF118. Component controls and training-time comparisons add evaluation procedures. These are reported setting changes; the PDFs do not establish which experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v4 adds reset ablations on QPSR/CQP and lookup-table and penalty-weighting comparisons on QPSR. It removes v2's MBD completion ablation and retargeting training-dynamics analysis, while narrowing the sampling-count sweep to ACOPF118 and reducing the noise-step sweep. These substantially revise the questions empirically examined.

E5.justification: Both versions report benchmark means and standard deviations without specifying repeated-run counts or seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Additional result entries do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many benchmark values change: DiOpt's ACOPF118 feasibility/gap are 86.60%/2.18% in v2 Table 1 and 84.33%/2.26% in v4 Table 2; its retargeting gap changes from 3.26% to 0.65%. Reported settings also change, preventing attribution to a same-setting method improvement. New ablation and runtime results, alongside removed comparison entries, substantially alter the evidence.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 and the reset-collapse derivation are retained. v4 adds Appendix B's multiple-sampling feasibility lemma and its total-variation derivation involving learning and discretization errors, substantially extending the theoretical argument.

C1.justification: The main DiOpt contribution remains intact. v4 emphasizes constrained nonconvex optimization, adds an explicit 'first successful integration' novelty claim, and softens the abstract's promise of rigorous constraint satisfaction to high constraint satisfaction.

C2.justification: v4 adds task-dependent explanations of training costs and revises noise-level guidance around optimal ranges for different sampling budgets. It removes v2's discussion of DiOpt's retargeting disadvantage under simple constraints and its DDIM warning. The central feasibility–optimality interpretation and general training-cost limitation remain.

D1.justification: v4 adds benchmark dimensions, constraint counts and train/validation/test sizes in Table 10, consolidated main settings in Table 6, DC3's 200 correction steps, Newton-completion details and measured training times. It also updates the software environment and supplies a project-page link. Much of this is newly documented information rather than an established implementation change.

R1.justification: v4 adds Kong et al., Yang et al. and Psenka et al., a multidimensional L2O comparison table, and substantial discussion distinguishing DiOpt from QVPO and relating supervised diffusion to RectFlow. This expands its research positioning. DiffuSolve's updated title/publication corresponds to the previously cited Li et al. work.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and generative-model discussion are extensively rewritten. Expanded preliminaries and equality-handling explanations, new experimental subsections, reorganized appendices, and revised title and baseline terminology substantially change the narrative structure.

P2.justification: The main text changes from one to two columns. v4 restructures benchmark tables around feasibility and runtime, adds comparison/configuration/ablation tables, redraws toy and sensitivity figures, relocates QP results and ACOPF118 dynamics, and removes older comparison displays.

improvement.justification: v4 adds useful tests of the reset, lookup-table and weighting components, plus training costs and data splits, improving empirical assessment and reproducibility. However, Appendix B infers likely sampling failure from an upper bound near one, which does not establish that conclusion. Its stronger positioning against RectFlow also rests on a supervised-diffusion proxy. These gains and new weaknesses in theoretical and comparative support leave the net quality change unclear.
